analysis.summary: Solid beat on revenue via a 20% surge in realised prices to US$74/boe, but underlying NPAT of US$1,334m grew only +7% as a 13% production volume decline and a US$559m cost-of-sales blowout (LNG trading, ammonia startup, Pluto turnaround) absorbed much of the price tailwind. Operating cash flow fell 10% to US$3,013m despite higher earnings, weighed by a US$419m hedge settlement cash outflow and working capital drag, making the profit-to-cash conversion the weak spot this half. The 57 US cps fully franked interim dividend (up 8%) at an 80% payout ratio signals confidence but also leaves limited room to repair gearing, which crept to 20.6% outside the 10-20% target. The single biggest forward risk is Scarborough first LNG cargo execution in Q4 2026: any commissioning delay would defer the material production and cash flow uplift the market is pricing in, compounding balance sheet pressure from Louisiana LNG spend.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- Revenue up 13% to US$7,446m on a 20% jump in average realised price to US$74/boe, benefiting from Middle East supply disruption; volume declines (production -13% to 86.5 MMboe) partially offset the price gain.
- Underlying NPAT of US$1,334m grew only +7% vs pcp: the Perdaman embedded derivative swung from a US$162m H1 2025 gain to a US$135m H1 2026 loss (US$297m pre-tax swing), hedge losses moved from +US$42m to -US$64m, and cost of sales rose US$559m, collectively devouring the price benefit at the NPAT line.
- Statutory NPAT of US$1,672m was boosted by US$507m of one-off DTA recognition (Pluto PRRT US$417m + US$90m US NOL); these are correctly stripped from the underlying figure.
- Red flag: operating cash flow declined 10% to US$3,013m while underlying NPAT rose 7%, a deteriorating cash conversion driven by the timing mismatch on oil hedge settlements (US$419m net cash outflow), higher production costs (+12%), and feed gas/processing costs surging 159% to US$238m.
- Free cash flow of only US$352m is materially supported by US$1,725m of Stonepeak/Williams Louisiana LNG capital contributions — on a like-for-like basis (ex-NCI contributions), investing-only free cash flow is deeply negative.

## Key numbers
| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating revenue | US$7,446m | US$6,590m | +13% |
| Gross profit | US$2,842m | US$2,545m | +12% |
| Gross margin | 38.2% | 38.6% | -0.4pp |
| EBITDA excl. impairment | US$4,647m | US$4,600m | +1% |
| EBITDA margin (on revenue) | 62.4% | 69.8% | -7.4pp |
| EBIT | US$2,157m | US$1,817m | +19% |
| Statutory NPAT (attributable) | US$1,672m | US$1,316m | +27% |
| Underlying NPAT | US$1,334m | US$1,247m | +7% |
| Bridge: statutory to underlying | Strip US$417m Pluto PRRT DTA, US$90m US NOL DTA (both gains); add back US$169m post-tax impairments (Calypso US$135m pre-tax, H2OK US$43m pre-tax) | | |
| Basic EPS (statutory) | 88.2 US cps | 69.4 US cps | +27% |
| Underlying EPS | not separately disclosed | not separately disclosed | n/a |
| Operating cash flow | US$3,013m | US$3,339m | -10% |
| Free cash flow (company definition) | US$352m | US$136m | +159% |
| Net debt | US$9,329m | US$8,657m | +US$672m |
| Cash | US$4,339m | US$4,880m | -US$541m |
| Drawn debt (interest-bearing) | US$11,370m | US$11,954m | -US$584m |
| Lease liabilities | US$2,298m | US$1,583m | +US$715m |
| Gearing | 20.6% | 19.5% | +1.1pp |
| Average realised price | US$74.0/boe | US$61.7/boe | +20% |
| Unit production cost | US$8.8/boe | US$6.8/boe | +29% |
| Production volume | 86.5 MMboe | 99.2 MMboe | -13% |

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion deteriorated sharply.** Operating cash flow of US$3,013m vs underlying NPAT of US$1,334m looks comfortable at face value, but the US$2,223m D&A add-back is the primary bridge. On a pure profit-to-cash basis (OCF vs statutory NPAT), conversion was 180%, but this is D&A-driven, not working-capital driven — the working capital movement was a headwind.
- **Hedge timing distortion is material.** The US$419m net cash outflow from hedge settlements in H1 is described as a timing issue — oil-linked losses cash settled ahead of related Q2-lag revenue recognition — expected to reverse in H2. This is plausible but investors should note it masked what would otherwise have been stronger OCF.
- **Production costs surging.** Unit production cost rose 29% to US$8.8/boe (H1 2025: US$6.8/boe). Total production costs rose 12% to US$749m on a 13% lower volume base, implying underlying cost inflation is worse than it looks. Feed gas, services and processing costs jumped 159% to US$238m (vs US$92m pcp) reflecting Pluto-KGP Interconnector volumes and Beaumont New Ammonia ramp.
- **Non-cash noise in earnings.** The Perdaman embedded derivative swung US$297m pre-tax adversely (H1 2026: -US$135m unrealised loss; H1 2025: +US$162m unrealised gain). This is a Level 3 fair value item with high model sensitivity — a 10% TTF price move swings fair value by ~US$178m. Management correctly excludes it from underlying but it remains a recurring P&L volatility source.
- **Deferred income release.** US$138m of other income from releasing Pluto Train 2 GIP deferred income (updated expectations that cost overruns/LDs won't crystallise) is a non-recurring benefit boosting statutory earnings. Not excluded from underlying, which is a modest framing issue.
- **Receivables build.** Trade receivables increased US$101m due to higher pricing, received in July 2026 per the report — a timing item, not structural, but worth monitoring.
- **Capitalised borrowing costs.** US$296m of borrowing costs were capitalised against qualifying assets in H1 2026 (H1 2025: US$340m), reducing the effective finance cost recognised in the P&L. This is standard for major project developers but inflates near-term EBITDA margins.

## Management framing
**Rating: Mixed — leaning Promotional**
- The cover page leads with "Disciplined execution" and operational metrics (98.7% LNG reliability, Scarborough 98% complete) before financial results — appropriate for an E&P but the ordering de-emphasises the cash flow decline and cost blowout.
- Free cash flow of US$352m is prominently featured (+159% pcp) without flagging that it is only positive because US$1,725m of Stonepeak/Williams Louisiana LNG contributions are added back in the company's own FCF definition. The underlying investing cash requirement is US$4,286m vs US$3,013m OCF — a US$1,273m deficit before NCI contributions.
- Production volume decline of 13% is attributed to cyclones, the planned Pluto turnaround, and Greater Angostura divestment — all legitimate, but the Wheatstone -30% (cyclone Narelle) and Okha FPSO -39% (mooring defect + cyclone) figures reveal operational fragility not prominent in headline framing.
- Unit production cost jump to US$8.8/boe vs US$6.8/boe is disclosed in the table but not discussed prominently in the narrative. A 29% per-unit cost increase is significant even on lower volumes.
- Gearing at 20.6% is described as "marginally outside" the 10-20% target, with three specific reasons given (lease liabilities, hedge settlements, receivables). The explanation is fair and transparent.
- The new US$350m annual cost savings target from 2028 is mentioned only briefly in the CEO quote — this is actually a meaningful development (implicit admission of cost base issues) that deserved more airtime.
- H2OK Project retirement (full impairment to nil) and Calypso divestment (US$135m impairment) are disclosed but positioned as portfolio rationalisation positives rather than write-offs of failed new-energy bets.

## Segments
| Segment | H1 2026 Revenue | H1 2025 Revenue | EBIT H1 2026 | EBIT H1 2025 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Australia | US$3,640m | US$3,854m | US$1,664m | US$1,473m | Revenue -6% (Pluto turnaround, cyclones, Angostura divestment); EBIT +13% (restoration provision reversal US$3m vs -US$443m pcp; lower D&A) |
| International | US$2,723m | US$2,170m | US$883m | US$469m | Revenue +25% (higher oil prices, Sangomar strong); EBIT +88% — standout performer; Calypso impairment US$135m absorbed here |
| Marketing | US$1,083m | US$566m | US$54m | US$144m | Revenue +91% on higher third-party LNG trading volumes; EBIT -63% — trading costs surged to US$871m (vs US$322m) and US$62m hedge losses hit segment; thin and volatile margin |
| Corporate | nil | nil | -US$444m | -US$269m | Loss widened; H2OK impairment US$43m; higher G&A; prior period included Louisiana LNG DTA benefit |

- **International segment is carrying the group.** Sangomar at 99.5% reliability, averaging 99 Mbbl/d (100% basis), is a genuine operational standout and Atlantis/Mad Dog both grew production. The International segment EBIT more than doubled.
- **Australian segment EBIT is flattering.** The restoration provision reversal in H1 2026 (US$3m credit vs US$443m charge in H1 2025) accounts for a large portion of the YoY EBIT improvement. Underlying production economics in Australia were pressured by higher costs and lower volumes.
- **Marketing segment margin collapse.** The expansion of third-party LNG trading is revenue-additive but near zero-margin or loss-making on a net basis — US$54m EBIT on US$1,083m revenue (5% margin) with US$62m hedge losses embedded. Management touts portfolio optimisation but this segment is not a meaningful earnings driver.

## Balance sheet
- **Net debt rose US$672m** to US$9,329m despite the period generating US$3,013m of operating cash flow — reflecting US$4,286m of investing outflows (capex + US$470m BNA acquisition completion payment).
- **Lease liabilities jumped US$715m** to US$2,298m, primarily the Woodside Bilangara LNG vessel and Trion construction vessels (US$655m of new leases in H1). This is IFRS 16 accounting but adds to economically real obligations and pushed gearing above the 10-20% target range.
- **Drawn debt fell US$584m** following early repayment of a US$600m syndicated term loan in June 2026. This is credit-positive, but US$800m of 10-year bonds fall due September 2026 — a near-term refinancing requirement.
- **Liquidity of US$8,189m** (US$4,339m cash + US$3,850m undrawn facilities) is adequate. Undrawn facilities of US$3,850m (up from US$3,550m) provide headroom.
- **Capital commitments of US$9,699m** remain (predominantly Louisiana LNG and Trion). Stonepeak has committed up to US$5,700m total for Louisiana LNG; US$4,262m received to date, meaning ~US$1,438m remains to be drawn.
- **Restoration provisions of US$6,813m** represent a massive long-duration liability; the unwinding discount accretion of US$156m flows through finance costs semi-annually. The provision did decrease US$73m in H1 from discount rate revisions and FX, a credit.
- **Goodwill of US$3,952m** (from OCI/BHP Petroleum merger) remains untested by impairment in H1 2026 — commodity price environment supportive.
- No covenant breaches reported; no material changes to financing facilities.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- Interim dividend of 57 US cps, fully franked, payable 25 September 2026 (record date 4 September 2026). Up 8% from H1 2025 (53 US cps).
- Payout ratio 80% of underlying NPAT = US$1,084m total payment. Prior half's final dividend of 59 US cps (US$1,122m) was paid in March 2026.
- Total dividends paid H1 2026: US$1,122m (prior year final); total committed for H2 2026 payment: US$1,084m (current interim).
- DRP remains suspended since February 2023 — no scrip dilution mechanism available to manage cash outflows.
- Capital allocation is stretched: US$1,637m net capex + US$119m exploration + US$255m abandonment + US$1,084m interim dividend = approximately US$3,095m of committed outflows vs US$3,013m OCF. The shortfall is being funded by Stonepeak contributions (Louisiana LNG) and balance sheet.
- The announced US$350m per annum cost savings target from 2028 is implicitly an admission the current cost base is too high; the 2-year implementation lag is unhelpfully distant.
- Browse pre-emption (US$225m upfront + up to US$175m contingent FID payment) adds further capex commitment not reflected in the guidance range.

## Guidance and outlook
- Full-year 2026 production guidance revised to 174-185 MMboe (prior: 172-186 MMboe) — range tightened, midpoint slightly lower. H1 was 86.5 MMboe, implying H2 at ~88-99 MMboe; requires Scarborough first LNG in Q4 2026 to hit top end.
- Gas hub exposure guidance of ~30% unchanged (3-year 2026-2028 average basis).
- Capex guidance unchanged at US$4,000-4,500m; abandonment US$500-800m; exploration ~US$200m; production costs US$1,500-1,800m; feed gas/processing costs US$500-600m.
- No explicit H2 NPAT or earnings guidance provided — standard for Woodside.
- Scarborough first LNG cargo: Q4 2026 confirmed on track. Post-period: FPU achieved ready-for-start-up and first gas — de-risks the schedule materially.
- Louisiana LNG: first LNG 2029; Trion: first oil 2028. Both on schedule at period end.
- Beaumont New Ammonia feedstock constraints (third-party construction delays) expected to continue into 2027, capping production at ~69% capacity in Q2. Lower-carbon ammonia (CCS-enabled) pushed to 2027.

## Positives
- **Average realised price +20% to US$74/boe** — strongest price realisation in recent memory, driven by Middle East supply disruption; full Q2 price-lag benefit flows into H2 2026 revenue.
- **Scarborough 98% complete, first gas achieved post-period** — the single most important near-term catalyst; successful commissioning unlocks material incremental production (~4.5 Mtpa LNG from Pluto Train 2).
- **Sangomar outperforming** — 99.5% reliability, 99 Mbbl/d (100% basis), reservoir exceeding expectations; extended plateau life reduces near-term decline pressure.
- **Operating cash flow US$3,013m** — despite the H1 hedge timing headwind, the underlying cash generation capacity is strong; US$419m hedge cash outflows are expected to reverse in H2.
- **Free cash flow +159% to US$352m** — positive FCF for the first time in the growth cycle (even with the definitional caveat around NCI contributions).
- **Pluto turnaround executed on budget and schedule** — zero LTIs across 400,000+ hours, critical milestone for Scarborough integration.
- **Stonepeak Louisiana LNG funding** — US$1,725m received H1 2026, de-risking Woodside's balance sheet exposure to the US$16.5 Mtpa project.
- **Capex 36% lower** at US$1,637m vs US$2,558m pcp reflecting Scarborough nearing completion and Stonepeak contributions — capital intensity declining.
- **New cost savings program** of US$350m pa from 2028 targets structurally lower operating leverage.
- **International segment EBIT doubled** on Sangomar strength and higher oil prices — geographic diversification working.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Operating cash flow -10% to US$3,013m** despite 20% higher realised prices and 13% higher revenue — the cost and hedge settlement drag is large enough to shrink cash generation year-on-year.
- **Unit production cost +29% to US$8.8/boe** vs US$6.8/boe pcp — the most alarming operational metric in the report; higher costs on lower volumes is a dangerous combination if prices soften.
- **Production volume -13%** — cyclone impacts (Narelle hit Wheatstone -30%, Pyrenees -39%), Pluto turnaround, and Greater Angostura divestment all contributed; some recoverable, some structural (field decline).
- **Perdaman embedded derivative liability now US$347m** (up from US$212m) — a Level 3 mark-to-model liability tied to 20-year urea/TTF assumptions with no observable market inputs; sensitivity of +/-US$177-179m per 10% TTF price move makes this an ongoing P&L wildcard.
- **Gearing 20.6% outside 10-20% target** — US$655m of new lease liabilities plus hedge cash outflows pushed the ratio outside range; with US$9,699m of capital commitments remaining, gearing is likely to stay elevated until Scarborough generates cash.
- **Free cash flow is misleading as presented** — only positive because of US$1,725m Stonepeak NCI contributions; on a pure OCF-less-investing basis the deficit is ~US$1.3bn in H1.
- **US$800m bonds due September 2026** — near-term refinancing requirement at higher prevailing rates; no new debt raised in H1 (zero drawdowns).
- **Beaumont New Ammonia running at 69% capacity** — feedstock constraints from third-party construction delays expected into 2027; new energy ambitions underdelivering.
- **H2OK Project fully written off (US$43m)** and Calypso divested (US$135m impairment) — two more new energy/exploration write-offs, continuing a pattern of capital destruction in the growth/new energy portfolio.
- **Marketing segment EBIT collapsed 63%** to US$54m on 91% higher revenue — hedge losses and trading cost surge point to poor risk-adjusted returns from expanded LNG trading activity.
- **NWS environmental litigation ongoing** — four court proceedings (3 Federal, 1 WA Supreme Court) could delay or impair the Chevron asset swap (expected Q4 2026) or future NWS operations.
- **No underlying EPS disclosed** — Woodside reports statutory EPS (88.2 US cps) but does not separately publish underlying EPS, making comparisons against consensus estimates less transparent.

## Bottom line
**Bull case:** Scarborough delivers first LNG cargo Q4 2026 on schedule, adding ~25 MMboe of annualised production from H2 2026 into 2027. This transforms the cash flow profile — US$3bn+ OCF could become US$4bn+, gearing falls back inside the 10-20% target, and the 80% payout sustains or grows. Louisiana LNG progresses on schedule with ongoing Stonepeak funding, and a sell-down of residual equity completes. Oil/LNG prices hold above US$70/boe on continued Middle East supply disruption. The US$350m cost savings program starts bearing fruit from 2027. Valuation re-rates as a growth-plus-yield story.

**Bear case:** Scarborough commissioning encounters delays (complex simultaneous operations across FPU, Pluto Train 1 modifications, and Pluto Train 2 are executing in parallel). Production volumes in H2 2026 disappoint, realised prices soften as Middle East conflict de-escalates, unit production costs remain elevated, and the US$800m bond refinancing occurs at materially higher spreads. Gearing pushes toward 25%, the board is forced to trim the payout ratio or suspend DRP reinstatement, and the stock drifts as a high-yielder with a deteriorating near-term free cash flow profile.

**What would change the view:** (1) Scarborough first LNG cargo timing — any ASX announcement of achieved first cargo removes the single biggest execution risk. (2) H2 2026 quarterly production report confirming ramp trajectory. (3) Confirmation of Louisiana LNG sell-down / additional equity partner at valuations supportive of the project economics. (4) Evidence that unit production costs normalise toward US$7/boe as turnaround costs and ammonia ramp expenses roll off.
